instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of 'communicates directly with' includes contact in person or by telephone, telegraph, letter, facsimile, electronic mail, or other electronic means, covering oral, written, electronic, phone calls, and emails.

Registration is triggered by expenditure/compensation thresholds for any 'person' who communicates to influence, without enumerating specific actor categories like law firms, consultancies, or public entities.
Chapter 305 defines several terms (e.g., 'person,' 'member of the executive branch') but does not define 'public entity' as such.

Coverage is subject to thresholds and exemptions, including minimum quarterly expenditure/compensation amounts and a time-based exemption (≤26 hours per quarter), which function as materiality tests limiting when registration is required.

Registration applies to communicating with members of the legislative or executive branch to influence legislation or administrative action, and those terms include legislators and executive-branch officers/employees (which includes the governor as an executive officer).
The statute targets direct communication with 'one or more members of the legislative or executive branch,' defined to include legislators and executive branch officers/employees.
The registration trigger is direct communication with members of both the legislative and executive branches to influence legislation or administrative action.
The law expressly covers communications with both legislative-branch and executive-branch members in defining activities requiring registration.
Persons must register when they communicate directly with members of the legislative or executive branch to influence legislation/administrative action, encompassing both branches.
Covered targets include 'members of the legislative or executive branch,' which includes legislators and executive branch officers/employees (including staff).

Elected/appointee officials are not required to register under §305.003(a)(2), and §305.0051 only allows the commission to require certain local officials/employees to file identifying information, not lobbyist registration.

The statute addresses public employees/officials by exempting certain government officers/employees from registration and provides a time standard (≤26 compensated/reimbursed hours per quarter) relevant to whether compensated lobbying activity triggers registration.
The definition of covered 'person' is broad and not tied to public charter or special governmental protection.
Registration requirements turn on communication plus expenditure/compensation/time thresholds, not ownership characteristics.
The statute does not define lobbying based on an entity's structure or revenue composition; it is defined by direct communication to influence coupled with thresholds and exemptions.
